questions.q: What four steps make up the CODE method?
questions.why: Lesson 1 defines CODE as capturing what resonates, organizing for action, distilling the essence and expressing your work.

questions.q: What question does the summary suggest asking when organizing a note?
a: How will this help move a current project forward?
How many words does this note contain?
Who else might want to read this one day?
Which app does this note belong in?
questions.why: Lesson 1 says organizing means saving for actionability, so you sort notes by how they support projects you are working on now.

questions.q: In the PARA method, which category holds ongoing responsibilities?
questions.why: Lesson 2 defines Areas as long-term responsibilities, while Projects are short-term efforts and Resources are future interests.

questions.q: Where do notes go once a project is finished or abandoned?
questions.why: Lesson 2 says Archives are where inactive items from the other categories are moved once they are done or on hold.

questions.q: Why does the summary say most note-taking systems fail?
a: They require rules that do not fit daily life
They store too little information to be useful
They cannot connect to the internet
They are only designed for large teams
questions.why: Lesson 2 says elaborate rules take time away from other priorities, so systems quickly become outdated and obsolete.
